item.title: Reading My Father's Poem '참회'
item.description: My father wrote a poem in Korean and called it 참회(懺悔), ‘Repentance.’ The full poem, followed by my short response.

item.title: quant-investment-platform — mid-retrospective
item.description: A mid-project retrospective on a personal automated trading platform built with Rust + Python + React. With ETF rebalancing and single-stock signal trading both in place, a record of how the safety layers — halt, block, detect, simulate — got built before going live.

item.title: Walk-Forward Analysis and Overfitting Validation
item.description: The structure of walk-forward analysis, the metrics it produces (IS-OOS gap, parameter stability), a momentum-lookback tuning case, and the limits that keep it from being a universal validator.

item.title: Korean Account Types and Investment Constraints
item.description: The core constraints of the four Korean retail account types — general, ISA, pension savings, and IRP — covering tax-free thresholds, tax deductions, the 70% risk-asset cap, and access to direct foreign investment, plus a strategy-to-account mapping.

item.title: Backtest Pitfalls Case Study
item.description: Concrete cases of look-ahead bias and survivorship bias — full-period momentum normalization, financial disclosure lag, close-on-close fills, S&P 500 reconstitution, the limits of free APIs — followed by an avoidance checklist.

item.title: Efficient Frontier and Portfolio Optimization
item.description: Covers Markowitz’s mean-variance model as the mathematical foundation for setting asset weights, the two optimal points on the efficient frontier (Min-Variance and Tangency), and the practical adjustments that compensate for the model’s weaknesses.

item.title: Microservices Architecture
item.description: MSA is a decision about which criterion to use to decompose the system. Domain boundary, data ownership, scale pattern, failure isolation — the chosen criterion creates the service boundaries, and those boundaries decide communication and data in turn.

item.title: Event Sourcing and CQRS
item.description: ES and CQRS address how a system’s source of truth is shaped and how its views are separated from it. Adoption cost spreads across the system, so I lean toward adopting only when the value can be stated explicitly.

item.title: Distributed Transactions
item.description: Distributed transactions are about how a single ACID transaction decomposes across services and how its pieces are reassembled. The roles and trade-offs of 2PC, Saga (Choreography vs Orchestration), and Outbox.

item.title: Claude Code Config in Four Layers
item.description: settings.json, CLAUDE.md, slash commands, subagents, hooks. Claude Code’s customization surface settles into four layers once you pick one axis: when does each one step in?

item.title: macOS Dev Environment: Dotfiles
item.description: alacritty + tmux + nvim + zsh + Claude Code in a single screen. The choices and structure behind a terminal-centric development environment.

item.title: I Threw Away My AirPods
item.description: A good engineer isn’t someone who knows technology well, but someone who can share that knowledge with their team.

item.title: Sensitive Data Encryption — Module Design and Migration Retrospective
item.description: A retrospective on column-level encryption of sensitive data in a running service. Envelope encryption, DEK granularity decisions, the WHERE clause constraint that led to HMAC, and the migration automation Skill that spread the work across the org.

item.title: Internal Hackathon Retrospective — 1st Place
item.description: A retrospective on the internal hackathon. How an idea I proposed evolved with the team into a 1st-place project and an internal launch — and the starting point for using AI tools in earnest.

item.title: JIRA Sprint Workflows and Git/GitHub Integration
item.description: Looking at JIRA’s issues and workflows as a graph of work units — covering the Sprint lifecycle, issue hierarchy, Git/GitHub integration patterns, and automation flows.

item.title: GitHub Actions Fundamentals — Workflow, Job, Step
item.description: GitHub Actions seen as an event-driven automation engine — the three-layer abstraction of workflow / job / step, plus the operational details of triggers, runners, and secrets.

item.title: GitHub PRs and the Code Review Cycle
item.description: Looking at GitHub PRs as a collaboration layer on top of Git’s change graph, and walking through the Code Review cycle, PR-level design, and merge strategies.

item.title: Git Workflow Basics — Commits, Branches, Merge vs Rebase
item.description: Looking at Git as a graph of changes — and seeing how commit hygiene, branching strategy, and the merge-vs-rebase choice are all decisions about the shape of that graph.

item.title: Security Groups and NACLs
item.description: How Security Groups (stateful, per-instance) and NACLs (stateless, per-subnet) form different layers of defense in a VPC, plus the common pitfalls each surface.

item.title: Connecting VPCs to Other Networks — Peering, VPN, Transit, PrivateLink
item.description: Comparing the four mechanisms that connect a VPC to other VPCs, on-premises networks, and external services — Peering, Transit Gateway, Site-to-Site VPN, and PrivateLink — across topology and cost.

item.title: Profitability-Based Traffic Throttling Retrospective
item.description: Retrospective on building a system that automatically identifies low-performing SSP inventory and throttles traffic to improve contribution margin. Covers the evolution from Imp Cost Ratio to a predicted contribution margin rate approach.

item.title: VPC Traffic Flow with Route Tables
item.description: How Route Tables decide traffic paths inside a VPC, the role of Internet Gateway and NAT Gateway as external exits, and the actual meaning of Public/Private Subnet.

item.title: VPC and the Isolation Model
item.description: How VPC simulates a private network boundary by combining IP CIDR, Subnet, and Tenancy. Includes vendor naming map across AWS / GCP / Azure / Alibaba.

item.title: Technical Indicators and Trading Signals
item.description: Covers technical indicators (RSI, SMA Cross, MACD, Bollinger Bands) for reading price movements, composite signal design, and a comparison of three strategy types across different time horizons.

item.title: Portfolio Management and Factor Scoring
item.description: Covers factor scoring methods (Z-Score, Rank) for combining indicators into a single score, plus the basics of rebalancing and asset allocation.

item.title: Backtest Performance Metrics
item.description: Covers the formulas and interpretation of CAGR, MDD, Sharpe Ratio, and other backtest metrics, plus five common backtesting pitfalls.

item.title: Momentum and Dividend
item.description: Covers the role of price momentum and dividend yield as factors in quant investing.

item.title: Valuation and Quality Indicators
item.description: Covers how to judge whether a company is cheap (valuation) and whether it earns well (quality) — formulas and interpretation of PER, PBR, PSR, ROE, ROA, and debt ratio.

item.title: Stock Data Basics
item.description: Covers OHLCV data as the starting point of quant investing, the difference between simple and log returns, and the meaning of market capitalization.

item.title: Zero-Downtime Data Transition Pattern
item.description: A three-step pattern combining dual write and fallback read to transition data formats in live services without downtime.

item.title: Envelope Encryption
item.description: How the CMK/DEK two-tier key structure in envelope encryption limits key leak impact and simplifies key rotation.

item.title: LR-based ML Lifecycle Retrospective
item.description: Building my first ML Lifecycle — a three-tier architecture for an ad Fallback CTR prediction — as a backend engineer without an AI background. The technical decisions I made, and what I learned through running it.

item.title: MLflow and the ML Lifecycle
item.description: Which slot of the ML lifecycle each MLflow component fills, and which pieces a lightweight team can pick.

item.title: Circuit Breaker
item.description: A Circuit Breaker’s trip trigger and recovery strategy must be designed together. Trip without recovery cuts the dependency permanently; recovery without a trip basis becomes meaningless cycling.

item.title: Rate Limiting
item.description: Before choosing a rate limit algorithm, the protection layer decides which algorithms are even available. This post lays out how L4/L7/Application layers and Token/Leaky/Sliding/Fixed algorithms intersect.

item.title: Ad System Outage Retrospective — A Shared Dependency and a Single Point of Failure
item.description: An external event drove ad traffic far above normal, triggering a cascading failure. The real problem was that the filtering component was a single point of failure — and the fallback sat on top of it too, so one collapse pulled both down at once. The fix took three paths: removing the fallback’s dependency (independence), adding rate limiting to the component itself (protection), and reconsidering the runtime (throughput).

item.title: Choosing a Model Training Framework: sklearn vs ONNX
item.description: sklearn and ONNX aren’t competing at the same layer. Once you separate their roles, the real question becomes ‘do I need an ONNX layer at all?’

item.title: Revisiting Logistic Regression
item.description: The structure and characteristics of Logistic Regression, and why an old model still holds the baseline position in CTR prediction.

item.title: The Blind Spot in Deploy Change Verification — Campaign Cache Incident Retrospective
item.description: The deploy was two days old, and the metrics had been calm the whole time. The moment we turned off the cache refresh batch, ad serving stopped. A retrospective on the missing verification of what a deploy actually changed.

item.title: Kubernetes Fundamentals
item.description: Container orchestration basics and what backend developers need to know: core objects, networking, scaling with HPA, and operational essentials.

item.title: Go Concurrency Model
item.description: Go’s concurrency model builds on CSP, providing Goroutines and Channels as core tools. An overview of how each works and when to choose what.

item.title: concurrency-go
item.description: A record of implementing and benchmarking three Go concurrency patterns — mutex, channel, and lock-free — to build hands-on understanding.

item.title: MongoDB vs Redis — Same NoSQL, Different Roles
item.description: Why MongoDB and Redis end up in different roles even under the same NoSQL umbrella. A comparison across data model, storage, schema, scaling, and use cases.

item.title: chat-services
item.description: A record of designing and building a chat system as a personal project to gain hands-on experience with Kafka and Hexagonal Architecture.

item.title: Spring WebFlux Fundamentals — Non-blocking I/O and the Reactive Stack
item.description: Spring MVC assigns one thread per request. When I/O waits pile up, threads sit idle. WebFlux replaces this with an event loop-based non-blocking model. A summary of the structural differences from MVC, the Reactor pattern, and when to choose which.

item.title: HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
item.description: HTTP/1.1 processes requests and responses sequentially. HTTP/2 changed this with multiplexing, binary framing, and header compression. A summary of the differences between the two protocols and gRPC, which runs on top of HTTP/2.

item.title: Docker Container Fundamentals
item.description: Covers container concepts, the differences from VMs, Docker’s architecture, and the basics of Dockerfile and Docker Compose.

item.title: Horizontal vs Vertical Slicing
item.description: The difference between splitting code by technical layers (horizontal) and by features or domains (vertical). Trade-offs and selection criteria for each approach.

item.title: Ad Fallback Server Design Retrospective
item.description: Designing a Nest.js-based fallback server while removing a legacy ad server. Why a horizontal layered architecture fit better than Nest.js’s default vertical module slicing for a single API with complex business logic.

item.title: Nest.js Fundamentals — DI and Module System
item.description: Nest.js provides a DI container and Module system at the framework level in the Node.js ecosystem. A summary of its core design principles: IoC, DI, Module, and Provider.

item.title: Layered Architecture and Dependency Inversion
item.description: Layered architecture separates code into horizontal layers by technical responsibility. A summary of the four-layer structure, dependency direction rules, and how DIP decouples layers.

item.title: Kafka Fundamentals and KRaft Mode
item.description: Core Kafka concepts (topics, partitions, consumer groups, replication) and the background behind KRaft mode, which removes the ZooKeeper dependency.

item.title: Implementing Hexagonal Architecture in Go
item.description: Core concepts of Hexagonal Architecture and its idiomatic implementation in Go using implicit interfaces and package structure for dependency direction control.

item.title: Builder
item.description: Builder is the answer when three limits of constructors meet at once — many parameters, some optional, and step-wise validation. With fewer than all three, simpler tools suffice. When the language provides rich named/default parameters, the need for Builder shrinks as well.

item.title: Factory
item.description: Factory’s shared intent is separating creation from use. The three variants — Factory Method, Abstract Factory, and Static Factory Method — split creation differently and suit different conditions. Static Factory Method is the variant most often encountered in practice, and DI containers absorb part of Factory’s explicit role.

item.title: Singleton
item.description: Singleton is one of the simplest patterns but the canonical anti-pattern debate. The decision to bundle single-instance guarantee with global access into one pattern causes tight coupling and test difficulty. DI is the general alternative that separates the two intents.

item.title: Dependency Injection — The Hierarchy of DIP, IoC, and DI
item.description: DIP (principle), IoC (pattern), and DI (technique) sit at different levels of abstraction. The hierarchy must be clear before framework features and design principles can be told apart.

item.title: Incremental Cache Refresh Pattern
item.description: A pattern for switching from full cache refresh to incremental refresh. Separating data by update frequency and applying change detection reduces network costs.

item.title: Cache Refresh Optimization Retrospective
item.description: How I reduced network costs and enabled instance downscaling by switching from full cache refresh to incremental refresh for campaign configuration data.

item.title: What RDB Transaction ACID Actually Guarantees
item.description: What each of the four ACID properties actually guarantees in an RDB transaction. A/C/D are relatively clear guarantees, but only I has ’levels’ — the gateway to the correctness vs. concurrency trade-off.

item.title: Two-Layer Control Loop for Ad Budget Pacing — Retrospective
item.description: A retrospective on moving ad budget pacing from a fixed-rule scheme to a two-layer control loop — per-campaign learning sets the baseline, real-time correction absorbs drift.

item.title: rust-server
item.description: A record of implementing the multithreaded HTTP server from Rust Book Chapter 20, experiencing how ownership and concurrency safety are enforced at the type level.

item.title: TCP and UDP
item.description: Two transport protocols that backend developers encounter constantly. A summary of TCP and UDP — connection establishment, reliability guarantees, flow/congestion control mechanisms, and selection criteria.

item.title: SwapDo Startup Story
item.description: SwapDo, a deepfake-based face synthesis meme service. A record of five months as a developer and team lead in a startup team.

item.title: Session Authentication and JWT
item.description: HTTP is stateless. Maintaining user authentication requires storing state somewhere. This post covers the structure, trade-offs, and storage strategies of server-side sessions and client-side JWT tokens.

item.title: 55L(GGS) Startup Story
item.description: A startup born from a casual League of Legends habit. From architecture design to desktop apps, a record of two people building a service that grew to 10,000 users over five months.

item.title: GDG Korea Android 11 Hackathon — YouTube Together
item.description: Entering the GDG Korea Android 11 Hackathon solo, building both server and app in three weeks.

item.title: KRIC Station Public Data Hackathon — Hidden Rest Areas
item.description: Korea Railroad Industry Information Center’s public-data hackathon. A three-person team built an Android app that surfaces hidden rest spaces inside subway stations, over three weeks.

item.title: About
item.description: Backend engineer. Writing about technology and lessons learned along the way.
